newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Nearly 200 China troops to be in HK before handover.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 200 China troops to be in HK before handover.

text.p: China will have nearly 200 People's Liberation Army troops in Hong Kong before taking over the British colony on July 1, the two sides agreed on Wednesday.
The British and Chinese reached the agreement in the latest round of expert talks at the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group, which is hammering out details of the sovereignty change.
Britain is returning Hong Kong, its colony for the past 156 years, to China at midnight on June 30, and the PLA will take over defence duties from the departing Black Watch regiment.
Under a 1984 Sino-British treaty, the territory will then become a quasi-autonomous region of China, retaining its capitalist way of life for a further 50 years.

In an historic first step, China brought its first advance party of 40 troops to Hong Kong on April 21, and spokesmen said 66 more will arrive overland from the neighbouring Shenzhen region next Monday.
A further 90 will arrive on May 30, bringing the pre-handover total to 196, according to the latest agreement.

Britain has twice that number of troops in Hong Kong at present, but that is a mere fraction of the British garrison in its heyday when it counted up to 10,000 servicemen. It has been drawing down its troop strength for several years now.
China has said it will match that peak strength eventually, although it was unclear how soon after the flag change.

Next Monday's contingent would move into various quarters -- the Prince of Wales Barracks in downtown Hong Kong, the Sek Kong camp in the rural New Territories, the Stonecutters Island naval base, and the Gun Club Hill Barracks on the Kowloon Peninsula.

"The purpose is to act as an advance party, to take over barracks, set up administrative arrangements, billets, beds, desks and so on. It's a standard administrative event," British army spokeswoman Captain Sarah Wood told Reuters.

They would drive into Hong Kong in 13 military vehicles through the Lok Ma Chau land border post, where their comrades came in three weeks ago. A small military liaison party would greet them and escort them to barracks, Wood said.

"They will get familiar with Hong Kong and the barracks that they will take over, liaise with the British Forces and the Hong Kong Government, and coordinate communications support and the movement of supplies," a spokesman said.
"As in the case of the first batch, the further batches of PLA advance personnel will not be armed and will not enjoy any special legal status or privileges and immunities," he said.
The first 40 PLA troops led by Major General Zhou Borong, Deputy Commander of the future PLA Garrison, are located with British Forces at the Prince of Wales and Stonecutters barracks.
China has promised it will send elite troops of the finest military fettle and highest moral calibre, and that they will be on top behaviour while in the territory.
However, many of Hong Kong's 6.4 million people have vivid memories of the PLA's actions in 1989 when tanks rolled into Beijing's Tiananmen Square to crush a student protest movement.

Britain has already shut its air base at Sek Kong, its naval base on Stonecutters Island and various barracks throughout the territory. It plans to sell off its remaining military helicopters and naval patrol boats used in Hong Kong.
A 12-vessel Royal Navy naval task force, led by the aircraft carrier HMS Illustrious and including the nuclear submarine HMS Trenchant, is in the area to assist with the British withdrawal.
